text:
maria: Quick one — I'm hitting an oddity in the gateway matcher. Two routes: one with host `*.example.com` -> service A, another with host `api.internal.example.com` -> service B, both with path `/v1/*`. Which route should match for `api.internal.example.com/v1/health`? I expected the exact host to win but logs show the wildcard handling it.

jonathan: By current implementation we sort by specificity heuristics: exact host > wildcard, then longer path > shorter. If you're seeing wildcard win that's surprising. Can you paste the route entries?

maria: Yep. Pasted below. This is in our routing config as deployed: 

```
- route: 
    host: "*.example.com"
    path: "/v1/*"
    service: "service-a"
- route: 
    host: "api.internal.example.com"
    path: "/v1/*"
    service: "service-b"
```

maria: Traffic from a canary node hit service-a for the exact host. I think the problem is we have service-label overrides that run at evaluation time.

kai: Are you using the runtime label-based overrides? Those run after matcher selection today, which is a known gap. If an override reroutes by label it can appear like the matcher chose wildcard.

sasha: We intentionally separated match selection from label resolution because labels can be dynamic (k8s labels, tenant flags). But that means precedence between static host/path and dynamic label rules is unclear.

maria: Right. We need deterministic semantics. Customers expect exact hosts to always take precedence over wildcards, even if labels change.

jonathan: Proposal: add an explicit numeric `priority` field on routes that overrides heuristic ordering. Default heuristics remain but `priority` can force order. Example: `priority: 100` for exact-host routes.

kai: I like explicitness. Two cautions: 1) defaults must be stable so rolling upgrades don't flip behavior, and 2) make sure `priority` is part of the route signature for rollout purposes (so we don't silently change traffic when updating other fields).

sasha: Alternative: formalize the matcher grammar: host-exact > host-exact-with-port > host-wildcard > path-longest > header-specificity > default. No numeric field initially, but strict rules make reasoning easier.

maria: Both ideas good. Numeric priority gives operators control for exceptions. Formal grammar is safer as a baseline. Maybe both: deterministic grammar with optional `priority` to break ties.

jonathan: Implementation notes:
- Keep the current indexing for fast lookup (host tree + path trie).
- Add priority as an integer on the route object default 0. During candidate collection, include priority and sort by (priority desc, host specificity desc, path length desc, header specificity desc, creation_ts asc).

kai: Sorting by creation_ts fallback is important for stable rollouts (A/B via create-order). I'd prefer `creation_ts` over `route_id`.

sasha: Also we need to update telemetry: expose which rule matched (fields: matched_route_id, matched_reason, match_score). That will make debugging these cases trivial.

dev-bot: rollout-checker: There are 3 routes in prod with priority != 0. Recommend audit before enabling priority-in-sort.

maria: Good catch. We'll run audit. One more: how do we treat header overrides? Example: `X-Target-Service: internal-bypass` could direct to service-b even if host is wildcard. That should be a downstream reroute, but currently the header matcher is part of primary selection.

jonathan: Header matching should be considered in the same precedence group as path specificity. So sequence: host specificity -> header match > path length. But if header is a dynamic veto (like tenant-based override) it should be an evaluation-time reroute. We need to distinguish static header matchers vs. evaluation-time dynamic reroutes.

sasha: Suggest adding `match_type: static|dynamic` to allow this distinction. Static gets considered in core precedence. Dynamic is applied after as a policy.

maria: Summarize action items: 1) Draft grammar doc for matcher precedence (host exact > host wildcard > header static > path length > default). 2) Prototype `priority` sort and ensure default 0. 3) Add telemetry fields to route events. 4) Audit existing routes for non-zero priorities. 5) Clarify static vs dynamic header rules in config schema.

kai: I'll take the draft grammar (PR by EOD).

jonathan: I'll sketch the priority prototype and perf implications.

maria: I'll run the audit and list offending routes.

ops-bot: Note: scheduled config rollout at 2026-04-01 02:00 UTC — please coordinate if you're changing schema.

sasha: tagging @product so they know schema may change.

maria: Thanks all, will follow up with PR links and audit results. :thumbsup:
